254	## 5. Record format for everything we fetch
255	
256	Every fetched item, from any source and any market, is stored in the same shape. This is what makes the audit trail and later weighting possible, so fix it **before** writing the first fetcher.
257	
258	| Field | Example | Why it is needed |
259	|---|---|---|
260	| `record_id` | `reddit-1abc23-c4` | Unique key, stable across re-fetches |
261	| `source` | `reddit` | Source weighting later |
262	| `category` | `C` | Category from section 1 |
263	| `url` | permalink | Traceability to the original |
264	| `fetched_at` | `2026-10-10T16:02:00Z` | Audit trail |
265	| `published_at` | `2025-11-03` or empty | Trends over time; our BMW feedback has no dates |
266	| `author_hash` | hashed username | Count distinct people, not posts, without storing personal data |
267	| `brand`, `model`, `chassis_code`, `model_year` | `BMW`, `5 Series`, `G60`, `2024` | Separate current car from predecessor and competitors |
268	| `powertrain` | `ICE` / `PHEV` / `BEV` / unknown | Matches the feedback files |
269	| `market` | `US` or `unknown` | Market is a first-class filter |
270	| `language` | `en` | Translation tracking |
271	| `text_original` | raw text | Evidence must be the original |
272	| `text_en` | translated text | Analysis in one language |
273	| `rating` | `4/5` or empty | Where the source has one |
274	| `engagement` | upvotes, likes, replies | Kept separate from mention count (reach is not relevance) |
275	| `content_type` | `owner` / `expert` / `press` / `news` / `stat` | Owner voice vs marketing vs opinion |
276	| `raw_ref` | path to saved raw file | Re-processing without re-fetching |
277	
278	Storage rule: save the **raw response first**, untouched, then normalize into this format in a second step.

282	## 6. Problems that will occur
283	
284	### Access and legal
285	
286	| Problem | Where it hits | How to avoid it |
287	|---|---|---|
288	| Anti-bot protection (Cloudflare, CAPTCHA) | Edmunds, KBB, Auto Trader, mobile.de, Autohome, Dongchedi | Start with API sources; scrape slowly with caching; drop the source if blocked rather than fighting it |
289	| Terms of use forbid scraping | Most review sites and forums | Check `robots.txt` and terms per source; record the check in the source config; keep volumes small |
290	| API quotas | YouTube Data API (daily unit budget, search is expensive), Reddit (rate limit, about 1,000 results per listing) | Cache everything; fetch by known video or thread ID instead of repeated searches |
291	| Unofficial libraries break | YouTube transcripts, Google Trends, app store scrapers | Treat as optional enrichment, never as a dependency of the demo |
292	| Cloud IPs get blocked | YouTube transcripts, some forums | Fetch from a laptop, store results, demo from stored data |
293	| Login or paywall | Facebook groups, Consumer Reports, parts of auto motor und sport | Skip; use free press summaries |
294	| Personal data (GDPR) | Usernames, profile links everywhere | Hash author names, never store profiles, keep only the text and metadata |
295	
296	### Data quality
297	
298	| Problem | Where it hits | How to avoid it |
299	|---|---|---|
300	| Wrong generation matched | "5 Series" returns G30 and older cars | Require chassis code or model year; tag predecessor explicitly instead of discarding it |
301	| Market unknown | Reddit, YouTube, forums have no country field | Store `unknown`; infer only from subreddit, language or site domain, and mark it as inferred |
302	| Duplicates and cross-posts | Same complaint on Reddit and Bimmerpost; one user posting ten times | Deduplicate on text similarity; count distinct `author_hash` |
303	| Reach mistaken for relevance | One viral video with 50,000 comments | Keep `engagement` separate; cap the contribution of a single thread or video |
304	| Sarcasm, jokes, brand-war comments | Reddit, YouTube comments | Classify owner vs non-owner; drop items without a concrete feature or problem |
305	| Marketing text mixed with customer voice | Press portals, sponsored reviews | `content_type` field; never count press text as a customer signal |
306	| Different rating scales | 5-star, 10-point, percentage shares | Keep the original scale and value; normalize in a separate field |
307	| Missing dates | Some review sites | Leave empty, never guess |
308	| Out-of-scope content | Recalls, pricing complaints, dealer service complaints | Filter against the challenge scope after classification |
309	| Translation errors | Chinese, German, French, Italian, Spanish sources | Keep `text_original` next to `text_en`; quote the original as evidence |
310	
311	### Technical
312	
313	| Problem | Where it hits | How to avoid it |
314	|---|---|---|
315	| JavaScript-rendered pages | Configurators, Chinese OEM sites, KBB | Look for the underlying JSON request first; headless browser only as last resort |
316	| Layout changes break scrapers | Any scraped site | One small parser per source; fail loudly with the URL logged |
317	| Text encoding | Chinese characters, German umlauts, French and Spanish accents | Read and write UTF-8 explicitly everywhere |
318	| Messy PDF tables | Competitor price lists | Extract text per page, let the model structure it, keep page number as source |
319	| Volume explosion | YouTube comments, Reddit | Set a cap per model per source up front |
320	| Lost traceability | Any source, if raw data is not kept | Raw-first storage rule from section 5 |

324	## 7. Recommended fetching order
325	
326	Ordered so that each step works on its own, and a failure in a later step never blocks the demo.
327	
328	| Step | What | Sources | Why at this point |
329	|---|---|---|---|
330	| **0** | Setup | Model and competitor config (section 2), record format (section 5), raw storage folder, cache | Changing the schema after fetching means refetching everything |
331	| **1** | Structured APIs | NHTSA complaints, Reddit, YouTube comments | Official access, no blocking, dated records, covers the US where G60 and G70 feedback is concentrated |
332	| **2** | News and press feeds | Car news RSS, CarNewsChina, CnEVPost, OEM press portals | Easy, gives competitor releases and the China view in English |
333	| **3** | App store reviews | Google Play and App Store for My BMW and rival apps | Easy, dated, per country, directly comparable across brands |
334	| **4** | BMW and competitor forums | Bimmerpost, MBWorld, AudiWorld, Tesla Motors Club, Motor-Talk | Deepest problem detail; scraping, so only after the pipeline is proven |
335	| **5** | Owner review sites | Parkers, Cars.com, What Car?, then Edmunds and KBB if not blocked | Adds ratings and the UK market for the F70 |
336	| **6** | Expert reviews | YouTube transcripts, Car and Driver, Autocar, comparison tests | Competition arguments; transcripts are fragile, so not earlier |
337	| **7** | Equipment comparison | Competitor price and option lists | Needed for the equipment-gap check against our option-list PDFs; manual effort per model |
338	| **8** | Market and trend data | KBA, SMMT, ACEA, Google Trends, consulting reports | Small volume, mostly manual download, used for weighting and assumptions |
339	| **9** | Native Chinese and other EU-language owner sources | Autohome, Dongchedi, 12365auto, Yiche, Caradisiac, Quattroruote, km77 | Highest effort and failure risk; only if time remains |
340	
341	Market reached by each step: steps 1 to 3 are the **shared platforms plus USA**, with China through English news and the App Store China storefront. Step 5 adds the **UK**. Steps 4, 6 and 8 add **Germany**. Native **China** owner voice only arrives in step 9. See [section 4](#4-sources-by-market) for the full per-market list.
342	
343	Assign the market to each shared-platform record (rules in [section 4.1](#41-shared-platforms-one-fetch-several-markets)) during normalization, right after fetching, so every later step can filter by market.
344	
345	Rules that keep this safe:
346	
347	1. Finish one source end to end (fetch, store raw, normalize) before starting the next.
348	2. Run each step for **one vehicle in one market first** (suggested: G60 in the US, the best-covered combination), then widen to the other six combinations from section 2.
349	3. Fetch once, cache, and run the demo from stored data, never live.
350	4. After steps 1 to 3 you already have complaints, wishes and competition. Everything after is enrichment.
351	
352	---
353	
354	## 8. Sources to skip
355	
356	| Source | Reason |
357	|---|---|
358	| X (Twitter) | Paid API, short low-detail posts |
359	| TikTok, Instagram | No usable API, mostly visual content |
360	| Facebook groups | Login required, private data |
361	| Consumer Reports full data, JATO, MarkLines | Paid; use their free press releases |
362	| Trustpilot, Google Maps dealer reviews | About dealers and service, not the product |
363	
364	Parked because the market is out of scope for now (add back when the scope widens):
365	
366	| Market | Sources |
367	|---|---|
368	| Japan | Minkara, Kakaku.com |
369	| South Korea | Bobaedream, Naver cafés |
370	| Middle East | YallaMotor, DubiCars, ArabGT |
371	| India | Team-BHP, CarWale, CarDekho |
372	| Australia, Canada | ProductReview.com.au, Transport Canada |
373	
374	---
375	
376	## 9. Open points
377	
378	- **Bias per source:** who posts there, which markets and owner types are over-represented. To be discussed.
379	- **Importance per source:** how much weight each source gets in prioritization. To be discussed.
380	- **Demo vehicle and market:** decides which sources in steps 5 and 9 are worth the effort.
381	- **China:** real Chinese owner platforms are in step 9; until then China is covered only through English-language news.

You're up to date with the remote now, and the fetching-sources file is intact but still uncommitted.

## Where the fetching-sources file stands

`data/05-web-sources/fetching-sources.md` is a complete 9-section draft (about 380 lines). I have no record of the earlier session, so this recap comes from the file itself:

- **Scope:** 1 Series F70, 5 Series G60/G68, 7 Series G70, in the USA, China and Europe (including the UK). That gives 7 model-market combinations.
- **Sections 1–3:** nine source categories (A to I, from owner complaints to future trends), the competitor list per model, and a source table per category with access method and difficulty.
- **Section 4:** the same sources regrouped by market, with rules for splitting shared platforms like Reddit and YouTube by market.
- **Section 5:** one record format for everything fetched, with a raw-first storage rule.
- **Section 6:** expected problems (access and legal, data quality, technical) and how to avoid each.
- **Section 7:** a 10-step fetching order, starting with APIs (NHTSA, Reddit, YouTube comments) and ending with native Chinese sites.
- **Sections 8–9:** sources to skip, and open points.

`data/README.md` was also edited to add the `05-web-sources` folder and a link to the file.

Still open in the file:
- Bias and importance weighting per source are marked "to be discussed".
- The demo vehicle and market are not chosen.
- API limits, URLs and terms of use are from general knowledge and not checked live.

An earlier pull had been left half-finished, which is why four files were sitting staged. I concluded it with a merge commit (`b70ebab`), which brings in the teammate commit `3ce8ece` ("architecture md files and more notes"): `architecture.mmd`, `data-model.mmd`, `meeting-notes-2026-10-10.md` and `notes ena w kechich.md`. There were no conflicts. Nothing has been pushed; local `main` is 3 commits ahead of origin.

I did not delete them; it may have been you, another tool or OneDrive. They are safe in the commit, and `git restore meeting-notes-2026-10-10.md "notes ena w kechich.md"` brings them back. If the deletion was deliberate, leave them and commit it.
